# Dakar Bitcoin Hack

Online Devpost hackathon hosted by Btrust. Goal: tools built on Bitcoin, Lightning, Nostr and AI that improve life in Senegal and Africa.

## Key facts (Search-summary)
- Deadline: November 20, 2026, 3:00 PM EST.
- Prizes: $900 in BTC total. 1st $500, 2nd $250, 3rd $150.
- Eligibility: reported as **students only**, no companies. Verify on the Devpost page.
- Must submit: presentation (text or video), a prototype/MVP/PoC, and at least a Bitcoin/Lightning wallet integration.
- Projects are expected to be open source and built in public.

## Judging focus
Usefulness and local impact is the stressed criterion. See [[past-winners]] for what scored well.

## Relevance
Shapes the scope of [[tontinesats]]: two weeks of build time, open-source code, and a working Lightning flow.

# Diaspora Remittances

## Costs (Search-summary)
- Global average remittance cost: about 6.3%.
- Sub-Saharan Africa: the most expensive region, above 8%.
- France to Senegal corridor: roughly 3-5%, lower because of competition. Check exact figures at remittanceprices.worldbank.org.

## Diaspora tontines (Search-summary)
- Senegalese migrants, especially women, run tontines in France, sometimes with contributions of hundreds of euros per cycle (UvA, OpenEdition).
- Digital rails let diaspora members fund cycles back home.

## Unknown
How many Dakar tontines include members abroad. This number decides how strong the cross-border pitch is. See [[risks-and-open-questions]].

# Differentiators

| Difference | Versus | Defensibility |
|---|---|---|
| Non-custodial, peer-to-peer payouts | [[matontine]] and [[zepargn]] hold funds through regulated partners | High |
| Cross-border by default over Lightning | Mobile money is national; diaspora members need a remittance step | Medium (corridor fees are only about 3-5%, see [[diaspora-remittances]]) |
| Portable reputation on Nostr | Competitors keep credit data in their own database | High in theory; needs a lender who accepts it |
| Open source, self-hostable | All competitors are closed | Medium; matches [[dakar-bitcoin-hack]] rules |

## Corrections to earlier claims
- "Zero intermediaries" is too strong. A member in France still buys sats with euros, and the beneficiary may convert sats to CFA. Both steps have spreads.
- "No licence needed" is a legal question that was not checked. Do not put it in the pitch.
- Self-published reputation is fakeable. Each payment record must be co-signed by the person who received it. See [[technical-building-blocks]].

## Related
[[tontinesats]], [[risks-and-open-questions]]

# MaTontine

Fintech that digitizes tontines in Senegal and West Africa, via smartphone app or SMS.

## How it works (Search-summary)
- Custody through regulated partners such as the microfinance institution COFINA, under BCEAO rules.
- Contributions and payouts over mobile money (Orange Money and others).
- Free for members. Revenue from commissions paid by partners (lenders, insurers) who use its credit-scoring data.
- Builds credit scores from saving behaviour; the data stays in its own platform.

## Gaps for [[tontinesats]]
- Cross-border members likely need a separate remittance step first (not confirmed).
- Reputation data is not portable.
- Closed source.

## Related

# Past Winners

Rankings come from search summaries and need checking on the Devpost page.

| Place | Project | Concept |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | GandalNexus | BitQuest (gamified learning) and BitLab (testnet sandbox) |
| 2nd | PaySats | Wallet bridging Lightning with Wave and Orange Money, plus savings vaults |
| Finalist | BitTravel | Intercity bus tickets paid via Lightning or mobile money |

## Pattern
Winners solved everyday local friction and connected to how people already pay (mobile money). See [[senegal-financial-inclusion]].

## Implication
PaySats already covers the mobile money bridge, so [[tontinesats]] should not compete on that. It should compete on group savings, see [[differentiators]].

# Risks and Open Questions

## Unverified facts
- Hackathon eligibility (students only) and winner rankings. See [[dakar-bitcoin-hack]] and [[past-winners]].
- The 90% / 64% participant figures in [[tontine]].
- Share of tontines with diaspora members. See [[diaspora-remittances]].
- Whether [[matontine]] already supports cross-border members.
- What [[kolonell]] actually sells.

## Product risks
- **Adoption.** Groups already trust each other; the tool must save the organizer real work.
- **Wallet onboarding.** Most target users have Wave, not a Lightning wallet. A demo needs a hosted wallet or a mobile money bridge.
- **Missed payments.** Non-custodial design means the app cannot force payment; it can only remind and record.
- **Regulation.** BCEAO rules on payment services were not reviewed.
- **Reputation value.** Portable records only matter if a lender accepts them.

## Related

# Senegal Financial Inclusion

## Global Findex 2021 (Search-summary)
- 56% of adults owned an account (financial institution or mobile money), up from about 15% in 2014.
- Across WAEMU, roughly 75% of account owners use mobile money.
- Senegal is above the WAEMU average (about 41%).

## Implication
Mobile money (Wave, Orange Money) is the default way to pay. Inside Senegal, Bitcoin does not beat Wave on cost or familiarity. The case for Lightning is cross-border, see [[diaspora-remittances]].

# Technical Building Blocks

| Block | Role in [[tontinesats]] |
|---|---|
| Lightning Network | Fast, low-fee payments from each member to the round's beneficiary |
| NWC (Nostr Wallet Connect, NIP-47) | Members authorise the app to pay scheduled invoices from their own wallet, with a spending budget |
| Nostr identity (npub) | Login without email or phone; owner of the reputation record |
| Signed receipt events | Beneficiary signs "I received X from member Y in round N"; prevents fake self-reported history |
| LNbits | Hosted wallets for demo users who have no Lightning wallet yet |
| CFA/BTC price feed | Converts the CFA contribution into sats at payment time |

## Payment flow
1. Round opens; the app asks the beneficiary's wallet for one invoice per member.
2. Each member's NWC connection pays its invoice, or the member pays by QR.
3. On settlement, the beneficiary's client publishes a signed receipt.
4. The app marks the round complete when every receipt exists.

# Tontine

A rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA). Members pay a fixed amount each period; one member takes the whole pot each round until everyone has received it once. Wolof names: *natt*, *tegg*.

## Why it persists (Search-summary)
- Fills the gap left by formal banking.
- Works as a zero-interest loan for whoever receives the pot early.
- Default rates stay very low because of social collateral, peer pressure and reputation, without legal enforcement (RePEc, Cairn).
- Participants are mostly economically active: about 90% wage earners and/or 64% in the informal sector, per one study (Emerald). Check against the original paper before citing.
- Women are heavy users, for trade financing and social security.

## Design lesson
Trust already exists inside the group. Software must not replace it; it should remove friction around it. See [[tontinesats]] and [[risks-and-open-questions]].

## Related
[[diaspora-remittances]], [[matontine]]

# TontineSats

## One-line pitch
A tontine you can join from anywhere, that never holds your money, and where your payment record belongs to you.

## Core design decisions
1. **Non-custodial.** Each round, members pay that round's beneficiary directly. The app tracks, reminds and verifies.
2. **CFA-denominated.** Members see "10,000 CFA". Lightning is the rail underneath; the beneficiary receives funds within minutes, so price exposure is short.
3. **Organizer-first.** The treasurer adopts the tool and brings the group. Members do not need to understand Bitcoin.
4. **Not an investment product.** Framed as a record-keeping and payment tool for an existing group.

## Primary personas (Assumption)
- Organizer: a woman market trader in Dakar who runs a circle of 5-15 people.
- Diaspora member: a Senegalese worker in France paying into a home circle.

## Related
[[tontine]], [[differentiators]], [[technical-building-blocks]], [[risks-and-open-questions]], [[dakar-bitcoin-hack]]

# Zepargn

Consumer savings app in the WAEMU zone (mainly Benin), by Digital Elevate SAS.

## Features (Search-summary)
- Group tontines, personal goals, locked deposits (Z-lock), microcredit (Z-flex).
- Mobile money gateways: MTN MoMo, Celtis, Kkiapay.
- Funds managed with AVM, a licensed decentralized financial institution (SFD) regulated by BCEAO.
- Free app; some transaction fees; 5% capital penalty plus lost interest on early Z-lock withdrawal.

## Relevance
Mainly Benin, so a weaker direct competitor in Senegal.

## Related
[[matontine]], [[differentiators]]
